title: A Group of Crows Is Called a Murder
fact: A group of crows is called a murder, possibly due to medieval folklore that considered crows as harbingers of death or omens of doom.

title: The Coldest Place in Universe Is on Earth
fact: The Boomerang Nebula holds the record for the coldest known natural place in the universe at -458°F (-272°C), colder than empty space which is -455°F (-270°C).

title: The Average Person Walks 5 Times Around Earth
fact: The average person walks about 110,000 miles in their lifetime, equivalent to walking around the Earth 5 times at the equator.

title: Honeybees Can Recognize Human Faces
fact: Honeybees can learn and remember human faces, distinguishing between familiar and unfamiliar faces with accuracy rates similar to humans.

title: The Eiffel Tower Can Be 15cm Taller in Summer
fact: The Eiffel Tower can grow up to 15 centimeters (6 inches) taller during hot summer days due to thermal expansion of the iron structure.

title: Russia Has 11 Time Zones
fact: Russia spans 11 time zones, more than any other country, stretching about 5,800 miles from Kaliningrad to the Bering Strait.

title: Mars Sunsets Are Blue
fact: Due to the fine dust particles in Mars' atmosphere that scatter blue light, sunsets on Mars appear blue instead of the orange/red sunsets we see on Earth.

title: The Heart Pumps 2,000 Gallons Daily
fact: The human heart pumps about 2,000 gallons (7,500 liters) of blood through 60,000 miles of blood vessels every day, circulating blood every 60 seconds.

title: The Titanic Sank in 1912 With Modern Consequences
fact: The Titanic sank in 1912, and all 1,517 victims died, yet it occurred during the 100th anniversary of the modern Olympics being revived.

title: A Cockroach Can Live Without Its Head
fact: A cockroach can survive for weeks without its head because its brain is not located in its head and it breathes through holes in its body segments.

title: LED Lights Are 90% More Efficient
fact: LED lights use up to 90% less energy and last 25 times longer than traditional incandescent bulbs, potentially lasting 25,000-50,000 hours.

title: Greenland Is Mostly Ice, Not Green
fact: Greenland is 81% covered by ice, making it the largest island covered by ice. If all ice melted, global sea levels would rise about 24 feet.

title: The Longest Bone Is the Femur
fact: The femur (thigh bone) is the longest, largest, and strongest bone in the human body, supporting half the body's weight and measuring about 26% of a person's height.

title: Butterflies Have 12,000 Eyes
fact: Butterflies have compound eyes with thousands of lenses, each providing a small image. They can see ultraviolet light that humans cannot perceive.

title: Water Can Boil and Freeze Simultaneously
fact: At certain pressure conditions, water can exist in a 'triple point' where it boils, freezes, and melts simultaneously, known as the Leidenfrost effect.

title: The First Message on Twitter Was 2006
fact: Jack Dorsey sent the first tweet on March 21, 2006: 'just setting up my twttr.' Twitter was originally called 'twttr' without vowels.

title: The K2 Mountain Kills 1 in 4 Climbers
fact: Mount K2 has a fatality rate of about 25%, making it one of the most dangerous mountains to climb, second only to Annapurna I.

title: The Heart Symbol Wasn't Always Romantic
fact: The heart shape as we know it appeared on ancient coins and art for centuries before being associated with love in medieval times.

title: Your Body Has Enough Iron to Make a Nail
fact: The human body contains about 3-4 grams of iron, enough to make a small nail. Most iron is found in hemoglobin, which carries oxygen in the blood.

title: The Sun Makes a Sound We Can't Hear
fact: The Sun produces sound waves that generate pressure waves through the solar corona, though these frequencies are far below human hearing range of 20Hz.

title: Komodo Dragons Have Venomous Bite
fact: Komodo dragons kill using bacteria-laden saliva and venom that prevents blood clotting. A single bite can bring down a water buffalo.

title: The Deepest Lake Is in Siberia
fact: Lake Baikal in Siberia is the deepest lake in the world at 5,387 feet (1,642 meters), containing 20% of the world's unfrozen freshwater.

title: Humans Share 60% DNA With Fruit Flies
fact: Despite 600 million years of evolutionary distance, humans and fruit flies share about 60% of genes related to human diseases.

title: The Internet Was Created for Nuclear War
fact: ARPANET, the precursor to the internet, was developed in 1969 to maintain communication during nuclear war by routing around damaged network nodes.

title: Cleopatra Lived Closer to Pizza Hut Than Pyramids
fact: Cleopatra lived in 30 BCE, the first Pizza Hut opened in 1958, and the Pyramids were built around 2560 BCE. Time perspective shows she's closer to modern inventions.

title: Your Brain Uses 10% While Sleeping
fact: The sleeping brain is highly active, using about 10% more energy than when awake. During REM sleep, the brain is as active as during waking hours.

title: Neutron Stars Are Extremely Dense
fact: A teaspoon of neutron star material would weigh about 6 billion tons on Earth. These stars are so dense that atoms are crushed into their nuclei.

title: A Group of Flamingos Is Called a Flamboyance
fact: A group of flamingos is called a flamboyance, reflecting their vibrant pink plumage. They often stand on one leg to conserve body heat.

title: The Amazon River Is Wider Than the Moon Is Tall
fact: The Amazon River's width can reach up to 202 miles (325 km) during the rainy season, which is greater than the Moon's diameter of 215 miles.

title: Goldfish Can Remember Things for Months
fact: Contrary to popular belief, goldfish have memories that can last for months, not seconds. They can be trained to perform tasks and respond to cues.

title: The Human Body Has 60,000 Miles of Blood Vessels
fact: If all blood vessels in the human body were laid end to end, they would stretch about 60,000 miles, enough to circle the Earth 2.5 times.

title: The First Computer Programmer Was a Woman
fact: Ada Lovelace, born in 1815, is considered the first computer programmer. She wrote algorithms for Charles Babbage's Analytical Engine.

title: Some Mushrooms Glow in the Dark
fact: Over 70 species of bioluminescent mushrooms glow green, using a chemical reaction involving luciferin and luciferase to produce this ghostly light.

title: GPS Satellites Have Atomic Clocks
fact: GPS satellites carry atomic clocks accurate to within a billionth of a second. Without relativity corrections, GPS would be off by about 6 miles daily.

title: Mount Everest Was Once an Ocean Floor
fact: About 450 million years ago, the limestone on Mount Everest's summit was part of an ancient seabed, compressed and thrust upward by tectonic forces.

title: Electric Eels Have Predated Prey for Millions of Years
fact: Electric eels (Electrophorus electricus) evolved electric organs over 10 times independently in different fish lineages, first appearing about 10-15 million years ago.

title: Water Exists on Other Planets
fact: Water ice exists on Mars, the Moon, and Mercury. Europa, Jupiter's moon, has more liquid water than all of Earth's oceans combined.

title: Your Brain Has 86 Billion Neurons
fact: The human brain contains approximately 86 billion neurons, each connected to up to 10,000 other neurons, creating a network of 860 trillion connections.

title: The Term Robot Comes from Czech
fact: The word 'robot' comes from the Czech word 'robota,' meaning forced labor or drudgery, first used in Karel Čapek's 1920 play R.U.R.

title: Lightning Strikes Earth 8 Million Times Daily
fact: There are approximately 8 million lightning strikes per day worldwide, with about 100 strikes occurring every second across the planet.

title: The Great Sphinx Has No Nose
fact: The Great Sphinx of Giza lost its nose sometime between the 3rd and 10th century CE. The popular myth that Napoleon shot it off is historically inaccurate.

title: Trees Can Communicate Through Their Roots
fact: Trees in forests are connected by underground fungal networks called mycorrhizal networks, sharing water and nutrients with each other through their root systems.

title: The Heart Beats 100,000 Times Per Day
fact: The human heart beats approximately 100,000 times per day, pumping about 2,000 gallons of blood through the body, equivalent to 5 liters per minute.

title: Saturn's Rings Are Mostly Ice
fact: Saturn's rings are about 90-95% water ice, with particles ranging in size from microscopic to as large as houses. They span up to 282,000 km from the planet.

title: The Human Body Has 37.2 Trillion Cells
fact: The average human body contains approximately 37.2 trillion cells, though this number varies based on body size, age, and how cells are counted.

title: Crows Can Solve Complex Puzzles
fact: Crows have demonstrated abilities to solve multi-step puzzles, use tools, and even plan for future events, showing cognitive abilities rivaling great apes.

title: The Roman Empire Lasted 500 Years
fact: The Western Roman Empire lasted from 27 BCE to 476 CE (about 500 years), while the Eastern Roman Empire (Byzantine) continued until 1453 CE.

title: Atypical Pneumonia Affects 2 Million Yearly
fact: Atypical pneumonia, caused by bacteria like Mycoplasma pneumoniae, affects about 1-2 million people in the US annually, accounting for 10-15% of all pneumonia cases.

title: The First Smartphone Was 1994
fact: The IBM Simon Personal Communicator, released in 1994, is considered the first smartphone, featuring a touchscreen, calendar, and email capabilities.

title: The Dead Sea Is 10x Saltier Than the Ocean
fact: The Dead Sea has a salinity of about 34%, compared to the ocean's average of 3.5%, making it one of the saltiest bodies of water on Earth.

title: Tardigrades Can Survive Extremes
fact: Tardigrades can survive temperatures from -272°C to 150°C, the vacuum of space, radiation 1,000 times fatal to humans, and pressures 6 times greater than ocean trenches.

title: The Moon Is Slowly Drifting Away
fact: The Moon moves about 3.8 cm away from Earth every year. In about 600 million years, it will be too far away to completely cover the Sun during eclipses.

title: Your Brain Shrinks While You Sleep
fact: During sleep, your brain physically shrinks by about 1% to 2%, allowing cerebrospinal fluid to flush out toxins accumulated during waking hours.

title: The Pyramids Were Built by Paid Workers
fact: Contrary to popular belief, the pyramids were built by paid workers (about 5,000) who lived in nearby villages, not slaves as depicted in Hollywood films.

title: Bamboo Is the Fastest Growing Plant
fact: Bamboo can grow up to 35 inches (91 cm) per day, making it the fastest growing plant on Earth. Some species can add 1.5 inches in height every hour.

title: The Deepest Part of the Ocean Is 7 Miles
fact: The Mariana Trench's Challenger Deep is the deepest point in the ocean at 36,070 feet (10,994 meters), deeper than Mount Everest is tall.

title: Sharks Have Been on Earth 450 Million Years
fact: Sharks evolved about 50 million years before the first trees and 200 million years before dinosaurs, making them one of the oldest vertebrate species.

title: Your Stomach Acid Dissolves Metal
fact: Gastric acid in your stomach has a pH of 1-2, strong enough to dissolve metal. The stomach lining protects itself with a layer of mucus renewed every few days.

title: The Milky Way Has 100 Billion Stars
fact: Our galaxy, the Milky Way, contains an estimated 100-400 billion stars, with most stars having planets, suggesting billions of solar systems exist.

title: WiFi Was Invented by Australian Team
fact: WiFi technology was developed by CSIRO's Dr. John O'Sullivan and team in Australia in the early 1990s, with the first patent granted in 1996.

title: The Romans Used Urine as Mouthwash
fact: Ancient Romans used urine as a mouthwash and tooth whitener because of its ammonia content, which acts as a cleaning agent.

title: The Human Eye Can Detect a Candle 30 Miles
fact: Under perfect darkness conditions, a human eye can detect a single photon of light. A candle flame can be seen up to 30 miles away on a clear night.

title: The Sun Produces Energy for 5 Billion Years
fact: The Sun has been producing energy through nuclear fusion for about 4.6 billion years and has enough hydrogen fuel to continue for another 5 billion years.

title: Octopuses Have Three Hearts and Blue Blood
fact: Octopuses have three hearts: two pump blood to the gills, while the third pumps it to the body. Their copper-based blood appears blue, more efficient in cold water.

title: The Amazon Produces 20% of Earth's Oxygen
fact: The Amazon rainforest produces about 20% of Earth's oxygen through photosynthesis, earning it the nickname 'the lungs of the Earth.'

title: The First Email Was Sent in 1971
fact: The first email was sent by Ray Tomlinson in 1971 to himself across ARPANET, selecting '@' to separate user names from host computers.

title: Africa Contains 54 Countries
fact: Africa is the second-largest continent with 54 countries (including Sudan and South Sudan separately), more than any other continent.

title: Humans Can Hold Their Breath for 11 Minutes
fact: The longest voluntary breath-holding record is 11 minutes and 35 seconds, set by Chile's Alessandro De La Vega in 2016.

title: Antarctica Is the Driest Continent
fact: Antarctica is technically the driest continent, with some regions receiving less than 2 inches of precipitation annually, less than the Sahara Desert.

title: Venus Spins Backwards
fact: Venus rotates in the opposite direction to most planets, including Earth, meaning the Sun rises in the west and sets in the east on Venus.

title: Bees Can Recognize Human Faces
fact: Honeybees can learn to recognize and remember human faces, using a method similar to humans by processing facial features holistically.

title: The Pyramids Align With Orion's Belt
fact: The three main pyramids of Giza are aligned to mirror the three stars of Orion's Belt, which the Egyptians associated with their god Osiris.

title: Your Brain Generates 25 Watts While Awake
fact: The human brain generates about 25 watts of electrical power while awake, enough to power a low-wattage LED light bulb.

title: The Longest Bone Is Longer Than You Think
fact: The femur is the longest bone in the human body, comprising about 26% of a person's height and strong enough to support 30 times the weight of the body.

title: The Sun Is Yellow Dwarf Misnomer
fact: The Sun is classified as a G-type main-sequence star, but it's actually white. It appears yellow through Earth's atmosphere, which scatters blue light.

title: The First Computer Bug Was a Moth
fact: The term 'computer bug' originated from an actual moth found trapped in Harvard Mark II computer relay in 1947, the first documented computer bug.

title: The Sahara Desert Was Green 6,000 Years Ago
fact: About 6,000 years ago, the Sahara Desert had grasslands, lakes, and rivers due to monsoon rains, before the Earth's orbit shifted and dried it out.

title: Horses Can Sleep Standing Up
fact: Horses have a stay apparatus in their legs that allows them to lock their knees and sleep standing up, though they lie down for REM sleep.

title: Honey Never Spoils
fact: Archaeologists have found 3,000-year-old honey in Egyptian tombs that was still edible. Honey's low moisture and high acidity prevent bacterial growth.

title: Napoleon Was Attacked by Bunnies
fact: During a rabbit hunt for Napoleon Bonaparte, King Francis I accidentally released thousands of rabbits that charged at Napoleon, who reportedly climbed a tree.

title: The Human Body Contains 206 Bones
fact: Adults have 206 bones, down from about 300 at birth as many fuse together. The smallest bone is the stapes in the ear, about the size of a grain of rice.

title: Atypical Pneumonia Affects Young People More
fact: Mycoplasma pneumonia, causing atypical pneumonia, most commonly affects children and young adults, often spreading in schools and households.

title: The First 4G Network Launched in 2009
fact: The first commercial 4G LTE networks launched in Stockholm and Oslo in 2009, offering download speeds up to 100 Mbps, revolutionizing mobile internet.

title: Africa Could Fit Inside Asia Twice
fact: Asia is the largest continent, covering 44.58 million km². Africa covers 30.37 million km², so Asia is about 1.5 times larger than Africa.

title: Dolphins Have Names for Each Other
fact: Bottlenose dolphins develop unique signature whistles within their first year of life, essentially names they use to identify and call each other.

title: The Moon Has Moonquakes
fact: The Moon experiences moonquakes caused by Earth's gravitational pull, tidal forces, and thermal expansion. These can last up to 30 minutes.

title: The Shortest War Lasted 38 Minutes
fact: The Anglo-Zanzibar War on August 27, 1896, lasted 38-45 minutes, making it the shortest war in history. Zanzibar surrendered to Britain.

title: Your Brain Uses 20% of Your Energy
fact: The brain, weighing only 2% of body weight, consumes 20% of the body's oxygen and energy, using more energy than any other organ.

title: Glass Is a Liquid With Extreme Viscosity
fact: Glass is technically an amorphous solid, not a liquid, though old glass window panes are sometimes thicker at the bottom due to manufacturing imperfections.

title: One Tree Produces 260 Pounds of Oxygen
fact: A single mature tree produces about 260 pounds of oxygen per year, enough for two people to breathe. It also absorbs about 48 pounds of CO2 annually.

title: The Great Wall Can't Be Seen From Space
fact: The Great Wall of China is not visible to the naked eye from space, despite the common myth. It's too narrow and follows terrain too closely to be seen.

title: The Moon Is Drifting Away at 1.5 Inches Per Year
fact: The Moon moves away from Earth at about 3.78 cm (1.5 inches) per year, and Earth's rotation is slowing correspondingly.

title: Electric Eels Can Leap Out of Water
fact: Electric eels can launch themselves out of water to deliver electrical shocks directly to threats, bypassing water resistance to deliver higher voltage.

title: The Human Body Has 60,000 Miles of Vessels
fact: The human circulatory system contains about 60,000 miles of blood vessels if laid end to end, enough to circle Earth twice.

title: GPS Satellites Experience Time Dilation
fact: GPS satellites experience time dilation from both their velocity and distance from Earth, requiring daily corrections by 38 microseconds for accuracy.

title: The Amazon River Flows Into the Atlantic
fact: The Amazon River empties into the Atlantic Ocean with such force that its fresh water pushes 150 miles out to sea, detectable by satellites.

title: Trees Communicate Through Fungi Networks
fact: Trees share nutrients and chemical signals through mycorrhizal fungal networks, sometimes called the 'Wood Wide Web,' supporting young seedlings.

title: Mars Has the Largest Volcano
fact: Olympus Mons on Mars is the largest volcano in the solar system, standing 72,000 feet (22 km) high, nearly 3 times the height of Mount Everest.

title: Cleopatra Lived Closer to Moon Landing Than Pyramids
fact: Cleopatra (30 BCE) was closer in time to the Moon landing (1969) than to the building of the Great Pyramid (2560 BCE).

title: The Human Body Glows in the Dark
fact: Humans actually emit visible light, though 1,000 times weaker than our eyes can detect. Emissions are brightest in late afternoon and dimmest at night.
